title: Match the money to the need, and get ready

say: Match the money to the need, and get ready.
This is the video for module 1 of Accessing Grants, Loans and Partnerships.
Growth money can come from four places, and each has a price. Your own savings or ajo payout costs nothing to repay, but it may be your safety buffer.

panel.heading: Four places growth money comes from
items: Your own money: nothing to repay
Grant: no repayment, strict rules
Loan: repaid with interest and fees
Partnership: someone supplies what you need

say: A grant needs no repayment, but competition is heavy and the spending rules are strict.

say: A loan is repaid with interest and fees on a fixed schedule. Miss payments, and you can lose collateral or your credit record.

say: A partnership is when a supplier, buyer or bigger business gives you credit, equipment, space or buyers. The goal of this course is to get what you need without putting your business or your home at risk.

say: The most common mistake is looking for funding first and deciding what to do with it later. I need money to grow my fashion business tells a funder nothing.

A strong need says what you will buy, what it costs, and the result in numbers. For example: two industrial machines, about 650,000 naira, so I can sew 40 uniforms a week instead of 15 and accept the two school contracts I turned down.
Question one. Will this need bring money back? New stock or a machine for orders you already have usually will. A fancy signboard may not.

panel.heading: Three questions that decide the route
items: Will this need bring money back?
How soon, and how much?
Can someone supply it instead of cash?

say: Question two. How soon, and how much? Loan repayments usually start within a month, so a slow return is a danger sign for borrowing.

panel.heading: Three questions that decide the route
items: Will this need bring money back?
How soon, and how much?
Can someone supply it instead of cash?

say: Question three. Could a supplier give you 30 days to pay, a buyer pay a deposit, or a cooperative share a machine? Then you may not need cash at all.

panel.heading: Three questions that decide the route
items: Will this need bring money back?
How soon, and how much?
Can someone supply it instead of cash?

say: And if the business is losing money every month, a loan does not fix it. Find out why first: prices too low, waste, or credit sales not collected.

panel.heading: Three questions that decide the route
items: Will this need bring money back?
How soon, and how much?
Can someone supply it instead of cash?
panel.rule: Never borrow to cover ongoing losses.

say: Hauwa runs a tailoring shop in Kaduna. A school offers her 300 uniforms at about 9,000 naira each, paid 50% on order and 50% on delivery. She needs a second machine, about 350,000 naira.
The order is worth 2,700,000 naira. Materials cost about 1,260,000.
The deposit of 1,350,000 naira covers all the materials, with 90,000 left over.
So the real gap is the machine: 260,000 naira.
Her 150,000 naira savings is her only buffer. A microfinance loan would cost more and take weeks. But the dealer agrees to 120,000 naira down and 80,000 a month for three months, only 10,000 extra.
She needed a partner, not a lender.
Funders judge you from evidence. Score yourself 0, 1 or 2 on these six areas. 9 or less out of 12 means fix gaps before applying.
For example, Funmi bakes in Abeokuta. Her sales go into a personal account mixed with family money, and she records no expenses. She scores 5 out of 12.
So she opens a business account, starts recording expenses, and works out the oven's extra profit. Fix eligibility gaps first.

panel.heading: Score each area 0, 1 or 2
items: ID, BVN and CAC ready
Business account with statements
Six months of records
Proof you deliver reliably
Costed plan for the money
TIN and product permits

say: Many people pretend to offer funding. Find the organisation's official website yourself, never through a link in a message. Check banks on the CBN list and loan apps on the FCCPC list.

panel.heading: Check that an offer is real
items: Find the official website yourself
Check the CBN or FCCPC list
Search the name plus "scam"
Ask who is paying, and why
Never pay a fee to receive a grant
Never share BVN, OTP, PIN or card

say: Search the programme name plus the word scam. And ask: who is paying, and why?

say: Real grant programmes do not ask winners to pay a fee. For example, Ifeoma was told to pay 15,000 naira to a personal account to activate a 500,000 naira grant. She found nothing on the official website and deleted it.
Never send money, your BVN, card details, OTP or PIN to anyone about a grant.

say: To remember. Start with one specific, costed need. Loans suit needs that earn money back quickly. A partner may supply the thing instead of cash.
Route every sale through a business account, so your statements speak for you. And never pay a fee to receive a grant.
